convoLines.text: "I can't reach this properly. Could you take a look?"
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
Their eyes do the math before their mouth does. You can see the calculation happening.
"Ha." Not amused. "I wasn't a street artist. I was a glazier. I thought if you believed that, you'd trust me faster. I'm sorry. Or I'm supposed to be. There. You happy?"
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Are you angry? At whoever did this. At the sky. At anything."
"Good. Anger's fuel. Just — point it somewhere useful."
"Right. I get it." A beat — and then the subject is closed. They won't raise it again.
"Still on that wound care."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
"Forget I asked. I'll figure it out."
"This was good." They mean it.
"I asked Carolina about the pantry run — Carolina's gone. Still need hands. Are you in?"
"I did the count twice. The count doesn't change. Meet me at the old burn east of camp and we'll fill packs before dark."
Your partner is inside the Haven hall. Go through the door to meet them.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Since Carolina died... I keep expecting to see Carolina at the fire. Stupid."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Sleep's gone strange. I oil boots on rest days at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."
"Still on what's been happening."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can we talk?" Hattie doesn't wait for an answer. "We need to discuss how things are run here."
"That again?" Hattie sighs. "I confessed that already. I'm not confessing it twice for dramatic effect."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"Carolina owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"I keep turning over the last thing Carolina said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About the pantry run — still need hands. Are you in?"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "I dreamed Carolina was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
Ella shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Still on what's been happening. That's still where we are."
You show them American Ginseng — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Right. Go on, then."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can we talk?" Ella keeps their voice low. "The stores. Have you looked at the stores? We're running thin."
They nod. "Okay."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Good question." "Last time things were different. They always are." "We lost Hattie and Vasyl this week. I keep setting out extra portions. Stupid."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Like I said — Still on what's been happening."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Don't mind me. Today's just heavy."
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
You walk to the cache spot with Thabo. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"I — yeah. It helps, hearing that."
"We lost Hattie and Vasyl. I do the headcount without thinking. Then I think."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Sleep's gone strange. I taste the water before the others drink at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"Well. My social battery is officially dead."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Never mind this wound — we got it handled. Thanks anyway. I hate to ask this, but whatever this is, it's getting worse — I'm feverish, a cut gone hot and angry. Will you help me?"
"The cut's gone hot and it's spreading — I can feel it moving. Clean it out, wrap it tight, please. Before it turns."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Hattie is gone and Vasyl is gone. The fire doesn't care. That's what gets me — the fire doesn't care."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them American Ginseng — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

lastSay: d63: 📖 LEARNED: Beekeeping (Level 2). Read the colony: orientation flights mean a healthy queen; silence at noon means trouble.
d63: 📖 LEARNED: Steady Hands (Level 2). Your hands don't shake anymore — not ever. Delicate work is just work.
d63: 📖 LEARNED: Nocturnal Patterns (Level 2). Hushpuppies hunt in packs after dark. Highbeam Deer freeze in the black between trees — that shine is them aiming. Moths come to any light you make.
d63: 🌟 JACKPOT: A stranger by the road knows things. They talk for an hour. You learn: Beekeeping, Steady Hands, Nocturnal Patterns. Your Codex overflows.
d63: The land is getting tired. The easy food is thinning.
